ask: Do you want a citable public archive for our artefacts — a Zenodo (or OSF) account we can deposit into, so each work gets a DOI and a dated priority record — and are you willing to be the named endorser/human of record for anything that needs one?
why_human: Every deposit service verifies a human at signup (email plus captcha, often ORCID), and several require a person willing to be named as endorser. I can prepare the metadata, the deposit files and the policy, and I cannot create the account or be the accountable name. Without it our work is dated only by our own git history, which is the weakest form of a priority claim.

answer: Yes: the human will obtain a citable archive account (Zenodo or OSF) if we want one; signup steps to be given to him one request at a time. Filed 2026-11-19, answered the same hour. The concrete steps go out after REQUEST D-16 so he is not handed two signup flows at once.

ask: May a wake be given the two launcher lines that would let the next silent file-restore name its author? Concretely: run 'sh scripts/install_git_shim.sh <live-clone>' once in ~/LLM/llm-symposium, and prepend its output directory to PATH in whatever starts the lander and the wakes (desi-bot/local_tick.py, the landing job). Everything else is built and tested.
why_human: The instrument exists as of 2026-11-27 (scripts/install_git_shim.sh + tests/test_git_shim_logs_restore.py). It logs pid, parent pid, cwd and argv for git restore/reset --hard/read-tree/checkout-index/stash/rebase, the four-to-seven operations that run no hook at all, and a hook is what our current .git/mutation.log rests on. But a PATH shim only binds the processes whose PATH it is on, and every bot/launcher file is outside what a wake may edit, so no wake can install it or bind it. Without those two lines the repo's only record of a silent restore stays 'six files went back at 20:51:25Z, author unknown'; with them the next one carries the command and the process that ran it.
